metadata.title: Measuring global education goals: How TIMSS helps Monitoring progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 4 using TIMSS (Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This booklet summarizes TIMSS 2019 results and SDG4-related indicators using TIMSS achievement benchmarks (Low International Benchmark) and contextual questionnaire information. It does not provide an analytic micro-data modeling workflow (e.g., no explicit student-level regression/ML estimation steps) and therefore does not specify whether complex survey weights or replicate weights were applied in the booklet’s additional analyses. For TIMSS analyses, the underlying TIMSS design is complex (stratified clustered sampling of schools and students), so analysts working with TIMSS microdata should use the official TIMSS sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the international database to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors. The booklet’s policy interpretation relies on benchmark-based percentages and descriptive comparisons across countries and grades, rather than reporting a specific weighting variable name or replicate method.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The booklet reports SDG4-proxy indicators (e.g., percentages of students reaching the TIMSS Low International Benchmark) and descriptive cross-country comparisons, but it does not document a PV-based achievement modeling pipeline or any explicit PV combining procedure. Missing-data handling is therefore not described at the level of an estimation method (e.g., imputation or deletion rules) because the booklet is a policy/communication product rather than a methods paper with reproducible estimation details. This is a reporting gap for methodological transparency, but it is consistent with the booklet’s purpose: summarizing official TIMSS 2019 international results and additional analyses without exposing the full statistical estimation specification.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The booklet uses TIMSS 2019 results at Grade 4 and Grade 8 (with a quasi-longitudinal design where some systems administered Grade 4 to fifth grade and Grade 8 to ninth grade). For SDG4 target 4.1 benchmark reporting, it includes only participating entities that took both the fourth- and eighth-grade assessments in 2019 (as stated for Figure 4.1.1). For other figures, it reports country-level distributions or percentages based on TIMSS 2019 student and teacher questionnaire responses and benchmark-based achievement indicators, but it does not specify additional microdata inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., missing-data case handling) in the booklet text.

data.outcome_summary: This booklet explains how TIMSS 2019 can be used as a proxy monitoring tool for Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4), focusing on learning outcomes and equity-related indicators. TIMSS 2019 is administered every four years at Grade 4 and Grade 8, with a quasi-longitudinal design that allows earlier cohorts to be assessed again four years later. The booklet reports benchmark-based indicators such as the percentage of students reaching the TIMSS Low International Benchmark in mathematics (and science/Earth Science sub-domain), and it links these to SDG 4.1 and SDG 4.7. It also uses TIMSS contextual questionnaires to describe early childhood participation patterns, gender and socioeconomic disparities (via parity indices), bullying prevalence, and school/teacher resources relevant to SDG 4.a and 4.c. Because the booklet is a policy communication product, it does not provide a reproducible student-level estimation pipeline (e.g., PV combining rules, missing-data strategy, or model-based ML performance metrics).
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a policy/communication booklet summarizing TIMSS 2019 international results and additional analyses, rather than an empirical ML study with a documented predictive modeling pipeline. As a result, it does not report an analytic sample size, PV handling procedure, missing-data strategy, or any ML algorithms/metrics that would support extraction of main findings in the ML schema. The country list is populated from the figures and examples shown in the booklet, but per-country analytic Ns are not provided in the text excerpt.
